summary: In Canvas Builder the CLI offers a narrower command set and refuses what is left of the wider one. internal/cli/sandbox_surface.go is the whole surface: ensureSandbox decides once per process whether Canvas Builder is in charge (sandbox.Required() or config.SandboxRequested) and, when it is, applySandboxSurface hides the six commands built on student data (roster, at-risk, to-grade, standings, audit-enrollments, since), the three that would change the token (auth set-token, auth logout, auth setup) and every command whose pp:path annotation is not course-traceable, then replaces the root command's Short and Long with Canvas Builder's own wording. sandboxPreRun refuses the same commands by name with exit 9, coerces --data-source auto to live, and refuses a webhook --deliver sink. root.go calls ensureSandbox from a help wrapper (help never reaches PersistentPreRunE, and help is where an agent reads what it may run) and calls ensureSandbox + sandboxPreRun at the end of PersistentPreRunE, after the --agent block, so a refusal's JSON envelope is written when it was asked for. which.go filters the curated capability index through the live tree's Hidden flags, so a hidden command is not advertised by a capability phrase either. doctor.go gains a sandbox section (mode, gateway, workspace, course_id, checks), rendered both in --json and, through renderSandboxReport, in the plain-text report, and suppresses the export-a-token hint. auth.go's not-authenticated branch and feedback.go's send path point at Canvas Builder instead. internal/sandbox gains MsgTokenSetup.
reason:
Decision D2: inside Canvas Builder this CLI is the course Canvas Builder has open and nothing else. The gateway already refuses student-area reads, other courses and outbound destinations, so none of this is what makes those things safe — it is what stops an agent wasting a turn, or an instructor's approval, discovering the refusal. An agent picks what to run from `which` and `--help`; a command that appears there is a promise. Offering roster and then refusing it reads as a broken CLI, and an agent that believes the command exists will keep trying variations of it.

Refusing by name is still needed beside the hiding, because the command list is not the only way a command gets called: a skill file bundled with an earlier version, a recipe, or an agent that remembers the name from its training all reach a hidden command fine. Hidden is discovery; the refusal is the answer.

The token commands go beyond the plan's list, which names only the student-data six. They are here for the same reason the auth hints were dropped in canvas-builder-refusals: ADR 0001 assumes a resourceful agent, and a CLI that offers `auth set-token` is offering to let the agent choose its own reach. Canvas Builder issues this workspace's token; swapping it is not a thing the agent gets to do, so it is neither offered nor accepted.

--data-source auto answers from the local store when the network fails. In Canvas Builder that would answer a question about the live course from a copy that may predate the instructor's last change, and the agent would have no way to tell which it got. live is the only honest setting when a gateway is the only source.
known_limitations:
Hiding is discovery only. A hidden command runs if it is named, which is why every hidden command that matters is also refused; the gateway refuses independently of both, and that is what the guardrail rests on. The untraceable-command hiding has no refusal behind it at all — those commands reach Canvas endpoints outside this course, and the gateway is what stops them.

A resource group carrying no pp:path annotation stays visible even when hideUntraceable has hidden all of its children. Cobra still lists the group in --help, and running it prints its own (now empty) command list. Left as it is because the alternative is a second pass that hides a parent once every child is hidden, and an empty group is self-explanatory where a missing one is not.

TestSandboxDataSourceIsLive asserts on flags.dataSource rather than on observed behaviour. The behavioural version would need the live source to fail in a way the CLI classifies as a network error, and neither half can be arranged: gatewaytest.Drop closes the connection, which surfaces as io.EOF, and isNetworkError (data_source.go) does not treat io.EOF as a network error, so auto and live propagate it identically; and gatewaytest.Workspace points both base_url and gateway at the live fake, so a dead port cannot be substituted without rewriting the whole layout. The coercion itself is the contract, so it is read off the flags, with that reasoning recorded at the test.

ensureSandbox swallows the error from config.Load, so a damaged config leaves sandboxProfile nil with sandboxActive true. That is deliberate — the surface still narrows, and doctor is what an instructor runs to find out why the rest is broken — but it means addSandboxReport has to tolerate a nil profile, and it reports "off" in that case, which is the one place the report is less precise than the state.

The curated-index filter in which.go keys on the live tree's Hidden flags rather than on rootFlags, because topWhichMatch calls resolveWhich(RootCmd(), ...) with no flags in hand. This keeps normal mode provably unchanged and needs no process-wide state, but it does mean `which` reflects whatever ensureSandbox has already done to the tree: a caller that reached resolveWhich before any command ran would see the unfiltered index. No such caller exists.
validated_outcome:
go build ./... and go vet ./... clean. go test ./... passing across all eight packages on darwin/arm64 with Go 1.27.1 (internal/cli 1.412s). go test -race ./internal/cli/ ./internal/sandbox/ passing. golangci-lint run --max-issues-per-linter=0 --max-same-issues=0 reports 0 issues in internal/sandbox and nothing in sandbox_surface.go or sandbox_surface_test.go; the touched generated files report only their pre-existing findings, plus one of the same kind on the line added to auth.go (unchecked fmt.Fprintln, matching every other Fprintln in that function). gofmt -l is clean on every file in this patch; it still reports helpers.go and sync.go, which is the generator's own formatting and predates this patch.

New coverage, all in internal/cli/sandbox_surface_test.go, run through runCLI against the gatewaytest fake. TestSandboxRefusesStudentDataCommands: one row per student-data command, each asserting exit 9, sandbox.MsgStudentData, refused_by "Canvas Builder", and that the gateway saw no request at all. TestSandboxRefusesTokenChanges: the three token commands exit 9 with MsgTokenManaged and credentials.toml is byte-identical afterwards. TestSandboxRefusesWebhookAndFeedbackSend [Review Focus 7]: --deliver webhook, feedback --send, and feedback with CANVAS_FEEDBACK_AUTO_SEND all exit 9 with MsgStaysLocal, against a real local HTTP server that counts connections and sees none; the feedback subtests also assert the note the agent wrote is still in data/feedback.jsonl, because the refusal must not cost the entry. TestSandboxHidesStudentDataFromWhichAndHelp and TestSandboxWhichOffersOnlyCourseScopedCommands: no hidden command appears in which --json or --help, and every match which does return is either annotation-free or course-traceable; the latter fails if a query returns no matches, so it cannot pass by finding nothing. TestDoctorReportsSandbox [Review Focus 7]: the sandbox section's mode, gateway, workspace, course_id and checks, with checks "ready" and "not set up" both covered, auth_hint replaced by MsgTokenSetup, no export CANVAS_API_TOKEN anywhere in the output, and "off" outside Canvas Builder. TestNormalModeSurfaceUnchanged: with OmitSandbox, six capability phrases still resolve to the same top match through the real CLI and --help still lists roster.

CodeRabbit reviewed the patch and raised two findings. The first, minor and valid: addSandboxReport wrote report["sandbox"] as a map, but doctor's plain-text branch prints only checkKeys and a fixed info-key list, so an instructor reading doctor in a terminal saw nothing of it. renderSandboxReport now prints the section after the hint it replaces, in a fixed field order because a map's own order varies between runs, and TestDoctorReportsSandbox gained a "without --json" subtest covering every line of it. The same finding noted that the comment beside the addSandboxReport call was stale — the auth block skips auth_hint in Canvas Builder, so nothing is overwritten either way — and that comment was rewritten.

The second, major and false: that sandbox.Required, config.SandboxRequested, config.Config.Profile, sandbox.Profile, refusedErr and writeRefusalEnvelope have no declarations, so internal/cli cannot compile. All six are in HEAD from Tasks 1 to 4 (sandbox-mode-config, sandbox-gateway-only-client, safe-retries, canvas-builder-refusals), and go build ./... and the full test suite pass. The review ran with --uncommitted --include-untracked, which shows it only this patch's diff; the same false positive appeared on the previous patch for the same reason.
